decisions.slice: I-4-4C4 (tracker #60): ONLY the read-only git merge-tree conflict oracle. The router already imports compute_semantic_ambiguity from this exact path; no wrapper, second module or schema is added.
decisions.oracle_command: The only Git command is `git merge-tree --write-tree BASE CANDIDATE`. Any non-zero exit is reported as ambiguity (True): a Git error is never read as 'no conflict'.
decisions.git_exit_codes: git-scm.com/docs/git-merge-tree EXIT STATUS: 0 clean, 1 conflicts, other = error. Measured with git 2.55.0: conflict 1, clean 0, non-git directory 128, nonexistent ref / all-zero SHA 1 (so a conflict and an invalid ref share exit 1). The boolean API therefore keeps the source rule `returncode != 0` and adds no conflict-vs-error classification.
decisions.object_database: merge-tree may write tree objects to the object database; it does not read or write the index, the worktree or any ref. This is NOT described as filesystem read-only. The tests use tmp_path repositories only and compare HEAD / branch / refs / status / index / worktree before and after.
decisions.runner_failure: A runner exception (timeout, OSError) propagates exactly as in the source; it is never converted into 'no conflict'.
decisions.no_push_capable_code: execute(), main(), argparse, GitHub PR/Issue reads, git ls-remote/fetch, replay, apply, commit, worktree create/cleanup and push / ref update are not migrated and there is no entry point.
decisions.byte_parity: Whole-file SHA-256 parity is impossible by construction (the executor is intentionally dropped) and is not claimed. Parity is per function (AST digest) plus the recorded intentional_diff.
